problem:
The entry ${a}_{13}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & k & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]$
equals $-\frac{1}{2}$ and $det(A)=k-2.$ Find the value of $k.$

$k=${{field-1}}
worked_solution:
First, note that we are given the determinant of $A:$

$$
det(A)=k-2
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{13}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{13}^{t}={c}_{31}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{31} & =(-1)^{3+1}|\begin{aligned}k & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}k & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =k+2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{13}^{′} & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{13}^{t} \\  & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{31} \\  & =\frac{1}{(k-2)}\cdot (k+2) \\  & =\frac{k+2}{\,k-2\,}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{13}^{′}=-\frac{1}{2}$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{k+2}{\,k-2\,} & =-\frac{1}{2} \\ 2(k+2) & =-(k-2) \\ 2k+4 & =-k+2 \\ 3k & =-2 \\ k & =-\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
